newsitem.title: USA: HORSE RACING-DERBY FORECASTERS PONDER ODDS, WEATHER.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DERBY FORECASTERS PONDER ODDS, WEATHER.

text.p: Oddsmakers of the horse racing and weather forecasting varieties were king at Churchill Downs on Thursday.

As people around the famed racetrack debated the wisdom of installing Pulpit as the morning line favourite over Captain Bodgit, everyone kept their eyes on the sky and their hands in their pockets as a cold wind blew in what could be a prelude to a wet 123rd running of the $1 million Kentucky Derby on Saturday.

The official forecast called for thunderstorms on race day, making it even harder than usual to predict a winner in the 13-horse field. No betting favourite has won the Derby since Spectacular Bid in 1979.

Pulpit was established as the 2-1 favourite by track oddsmaker Mike Battaglia even though Captain Bodgit soundly defeated Pulpit in this year's Florida Derby. Battaglia said he based the decision on Pulpit's most recent work, a win in the Blue Grass stakes at nearby Keenland and some solid workouts at the Downs.

Barry Irwin, the president of the Team Valour syndicate that owns Bodgit, disagreed, saying he thought his horse would be favoured by the time the starting gate opened for the 1 1/4 mile race for 3-year-olds.
And Bodgit's trainer, Gary Capuano, said he felt the fact that the horse was based in Maryland had something to do with the 5-2 odds. "Maryland horses don't get all the respect they should," he said.

Pulpit is based in Kentucky and owned by the powerful Claiborne Farm, which has bred 12 horses that have finished in the top three in the Derby, winning with Swale in 1984 and Johnstown in 1939, and raised numerous other stars, including Secretariat and Bold Ruler.

Pulpit and Bodgit had light workouts in the morning chill and their trainers pronounced them fit. The other top favourites, 5-1 Silver Charm, 8-1 Free House, 8-1 Concerto and 10-1 Crypto Star, went through morning exercise without incident.
"If I were the oddsmaker, I have them all at 2-1," said Capuano. "There probably will be no runaway with this race."
"It's always a rider's race nd there's no way you can really fully prepare for what happens in the Derby," said Frank Brothers, trainer of Pulpit.
